analysis.investment_thesis: MSTC scores well on Return on Capital (~30%) but fails the Magic Formula's equally critical cheapness test — Earnings Yield of ~5.8% (EBIT INR 178 Cr / EV INR 3,089 Cr) is below the 6% minimum, and revenue has collapsed 90% over 9 years. The business is being kept alive by "Other Income" (INR 340 Cr in FY25) that now exceeds core revenue (INR 311 Cr), making reported profits fundamentally unreliable for valuation.
key_strengths: High Return on Capital: EBIT/Invested Capital ~29.8% (830+145-378=597 Cr invested capital), well above the 25% 'excellent' threshold
Near-zero leverage: D/E of 0.17 with INR 378 Cr cash vs INR 145 Cr debt — strong balance sheet buffer
Asset-light e-auction platform economics: near-100% gross margins and 54% operating margins on whatever revenue it retains
key_risks: Catastrophic revenue decline: -22.9% CAGR over 9 years (INR 3,225 Cr → INR 311 Cr) — the core business has effectively collapsed
Earnings driven by 'Other Income' (INR 340 Cr FY25 vs INR 178 Cr EBIT) — interest/investment income masks operating weakness and is not durable
Extreme earnings volatility: operating income has been negative in 5 of the last 10 years, making normalized EBIT nearly impossible to compute reliably
red_flags: Other Income (INR 340 Cr) exceeds core revenue (INR 311 Cr) — Magic Formula EBIT is being artificially inflated if other income bleeds into reported metrics
P/S ratio of 9.78x on structurally shrinking revenue is dangerous; if revenue continues falling, this multiple re-rates violently
Free cash flow was deeply negative in FY24 (-INR 390 Cr) and recovering only partially in FY25 (INR 236 Cr) — inconsistent FCF generation
Net Profit (INR 407 Cr) is 2.3x EBIT (INR 178 Cr) — a massive divergence that screams non-operating income dependency, not business quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on MSTC: Earnings Yield = EBIT / EV = INR 178 Cr / (3,322 + 145 - 378) = 178/3,089 = 5.8% — below the 6% floor and far from the 12%+ target. Return on Capital = EBIT / Invested Capital = 178/597 Cr = ~29.8% — genuinely excellent. The problem is the Magic Formula demands BOTH metrics to be high simultaneously. Here, one passes and one fails, producing a mediocre combined rank. At P/E 14.6x the stock appears superficially cheap, but that P/E is computed on INR 407 Cr net profit, which is padded by INR 340 Cr "Other Income." Strip that out and you're paying 18-20x true operating earnings — not cheap.

The structural story is deeply troubling. Revenue has fallen from INR 3,225 Cr (2016) to INR 311 Cr (2025), an almost total hollowing-out of the trading/marketing segment. MSTC is a PSU (GoI promoter at 64.75%) pivoting to fee-based e-auctions, but the scale of that pivot is tiny relative to what was lost. The GoI backing provides stability but also limits the upside optionality a private operator could capture. Until the e-commerce segment demonstrates consistent and growing EBIT without relying on treasury/investment income, the Magic Formula cannot endorse this at current prices.
